prompt: Move between characters and their numeric codes: codeOf returns the int code of a char, and charOf casts an int code back to the character it encodes.
explanation: Every char is stored as a 16-bit unsigned number, so assigning or returning a char where an int is expected widens automatically -- return c is enough, and 'A' becomes 65. Going the other way is a narrowing conversion, so Java demands an explicit (char) cast: return (char) code. This two-way relationship is why character arithmetic like c - 'a' works.
hints: char to int is a widening conversion: simply return c and Java converts it.
int to char is narrowing, so the compiler requires (char) code.
'A' is 65 and 'a' is 97 -- lowercase codes sit exactly 32 above uppercase.
